response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view (PA). Study date not verified.
CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Not provided in findings.
COMPARISON: Prior chest radiograph, PA. Study date not verified.
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Difference from prior: the current image has slightly higher contrast and penetration, and the breast shadows and left chest wall soft tissues lie differently. This limits confident calls of true change in fine right lower zone markings and subtle lower zone density under the breast shadows.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None marked time-sensitive. Listed first for review, in order: F6 right hilar and infrahilar fullness (indeterminate; the two reads disagreed), then F2 right lower zone linear markings (indeterminate).

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central with slight rightward deviation at the aortic arch, within normal. Carina and main bronchi not narrowed. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, mass or band-like collapse. Coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone are more conspicuous than on the prior (F2, indeterminate; both reads indeterminate, technique may explain the difference). A tiny dense focus projects over the right lower zone on the current; see CAN'T DETERMINE. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides.
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle prominent, consistent with an unfolded aorta, similar to prior (F3). Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortopulmonary window not filled in. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior, indeterminate (F6). The two blind reads disagreed: one read did not identify it and the other called it indeterminate. Size change is not comparable between the studies. Left hilum not enlarged.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Right costophrenic angle sharp. Left costophrenic angle appears sharp and is partly overlapped by breast shadow. No visible pleural thickening.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette within normal limits on PA, with clear borders, similar to prior (F4).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion seen at this resolution. Clavicles and shoulders intact. Mild curvature and degenerative change of the visible spine. Both breast shadows present. No soft tissue gas.
- Devices: Left chest wall implanted device with arcing tubing and a small metallic component over the left mid zone, consistent with an implanted venous access device. Present on both studies, no new device (F1). The central catheter course and tip are not confidently traced.
- Below diaphragm: Both domes well defined, right slightly higher than left. Gastric bubble under the left dome. Several gas-filled bowel loops in the left upper abdomen, more than on the prior, indeterminate (F5). The reads disagreed: only one read identified it, as indeterminate. No free gas under either dome.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Right hilar and infrahilar fullness more conspicuous, indeterminate, reads disagreed (F6). Right lower zone linear markings more conspicuous, indeterminate (F2). Tiny dense right lower zone focus on the current, not clearly seen on the prior (see CAN'T DETERMINE). More left upper abdominal bowel gas, indeterminate, reads disagreed (F5). The device component projects over a higher rib level on the current; true migration cannot be judged because soft tissue and breast position differ.
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle and upper mediastinal contour (F3). Cardiac silhouette (F4). Implanted venous access device present on both studies, no new device (F1). Left hilum not enlarged on either study.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current a true nodule, for example a calcified granuloma, or a vessel end-on? | Reason: The focus is very small, sits among crossing vessels, and is not clearly visible on the prior, which has lower contrast. A frontal film does not separate a small nodule from a vessel end-on or a bone island. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest.
- Is the increased conspicuity of the right lower zone markings a true interval change? | Reason: The current image has higher contrast and a different breast shadow position, both of which make markings look more prominent. | Recommend: Correlate clinically. Short-interval repeat PA and lateral, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Where is the catheter tip of the left chest wall device, and has the device moved? | Reason: The central course of the tubing is not traceable through the mediastinum at this resolution. The metallic component projects at a different rib level on the two films, which soft tissue and breast positioning might explain. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing for lines. Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically.
- Is there a small left pleural effusion or a subtle left lower zone opacity? | Reason: Breast shadow overlaps the left costophrenic region and lower zone on both films, and there is no lateral view. | Recommend: Lateral view if clinically relevant.
- Are there subtle lesions in the ribs or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail such as pedicles and small lucent lesions is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.
- Is the right hilar and infrahilar fullness a real interval change, such as enlarged nodes or a hilar mass, or prominent vessels made more conspicuous by technique? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessels from nodes or mass. The current is sharper and at deeper inspiration than the prior. The two reads disagreed on this finding. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast. A lateral view would help if CT is not immediately available.
- Is the small dense nodular focus over the medial right lower zone on the current a true lung nodule, a calcified granuloma, or a vessel seen end-on? | Reason: It is a small focus on X-ray within crowded bronchovascular markings and breast shadow, and no definite matching focus is seen at the same site on the softer prior image. | Recommend: CT chest.
- Are the more conspicuous right lower zone linear markings a true interstitial change? | Reason: The current is sharper and slightly different in exposure and inspiration, and breast shadow overlies the region on both films. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If the difference persists there, CT chest.
- Where is the port catheter tip, and has the port or catheter moved? | Reason: The catheter tip cannot be traced over the mediastinum at this image resolution. The different projected level of the reservoir may reflect arm and breast position only. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing to trace the catheter to its tip. Add a lateral view if tip position remains unclear.
- Is the heterogeneous texture of the left humeral head a bone lesion or a normal or degenerative appearance? | Reason: The images are low resolution and the shoulder is at the edge of a chest film, so fine bone detail is unreliable. The appearance is similar on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the appearance persists.

IMPRESSION:
1. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness, more conspicuous than on the prior, indeterminate. The two reads disagreed. Nodes or mass versus prominent vessels cannot be separated on this frontal film (F6).
2. More conspicuous coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone, indeterminate. Technique differences may account for this (F2).
3. Tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current, undetermined: nodule versus vessel end-on.
4. Left chest wall implanted venous access device present on both studies, no new device. Tip position and possible migration cannot be determined (F1).
5. More left upper abdominal bowel gas, indeterminate, reads disagreed. No free gas under either dome (F5).
6. No definite lung mass, confluent opacity, right pleural effusion or destructive rib lesion. Upper mediastinum not widened. Left costophrenic region partly hidden by breast shadow.
7. Prominent aortic knuckle (F3) and cardiac silhouette within normal limits (F4), both similar to prior.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the right hilar and infrahilar fullness (F6). Interval not specified in the findings. A lateral view if CT is not immediately available.
- CT chest for the tiny right lower zone focus and the right lower zone markings (F2) if they persist on source image review in PACS. Interval not specified in the findings.
- Review the source images in PACS, with windowing for the device and catheter tip and on bone settings. Add a lateral view if tip position or the left costophrenic region matters clinically.
- Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the left humeral head appearance persists.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
